research_caveat: IMPORTANT: the sandbox network gateway (agent proxy) returned 403 CONNECT denials for replicate.com, internal.replicate.com, archive.org and web.archive.org in this session, so NO Replicate page could be fetched directly (WebFetch and curl both failed). Every value below is sourced from Replicate's own pages as surfaced verbatim in domain-restricted web-search snippets (allowed_domains limited to replicate.com). Per researcher hard rules, confidence is therefore capped at 'low' even where the underlying Replicate page is unambiguous. The verifier pass should re-fetch each source_url from an unrestricted network before values are promoted. ADDITIONAL ENTITY CAVEAT: Replicate publicly announced it is joining Cloudflare (https://replicate.com/blog/replicate-cloudflare); its Terms of Service and privacy policy now name 'Replicate, LLC' (historically the company was 'Replicate, Inc.'), consistent with a post-acquisition entity conversion. The exact current legal entity and its relationship to Cloudflare, Inc. must be confirmed with the vendor and reconciled against Tavus's TOM questionnaire #8.3 (no TOM file exists in this repo).

The field playbook requires this to match the entity named in TOM questionnaire #8.3 that Tavus already submitted — no TOM questionnaire file exists in this repo, so the filler/human must reconcile before writing the cell. 3.1.1.locator: Shared network vulnerability disclosure (blog, May 2024): 'since February 20th, all internal traffic from model pods is encrypted using TLS'; mitigations included 'encrypting all internal traffic and restricting privileged network access for all model containers'. The public API (api.replicate.com) is served over HTTPS (replicate.com/docs/reference/http).
3.1.1.notes: Real standard: TLS/HTTPS — the negotiated TLS VERSION (1.2 vs 1.3) is not published anywhere retrieved this session, so per the form rule the dropdown must be 'Others - pls indicate below' with 'TLS (version not publicly documented; vendor confirms internal pod traffic TLS-encrypted since 2024-02-20)' in the free-text row. Do NOT write 'TLS 1.2'/'TLS 1.3' without vendor confirmation. Snippet-sourced; direct fetch blocked. An empirical TLS handshake against api.replicate.com was impossible (gateway blocks CONNECT).

3.1.2.notes: No Replicate primary source retrieved this session states an encryption-at-rest standard for customer data (inputs, outputs, files, model weights). The Enterprise page mentions 'strict controls for... encryption' without specifics. Replicate runs on hyperscaler infrastructure (its published subprocessor list is at replicate.com/docs/topics/site-policy/subprocessors, contents not retrievable this session), but inferring the underlying cloud's AES-256 default would violate the no-inference rule. Searched: replicate.com/enterprise, /privacy, /terms, /docs (security, data-retention, secrets pages) via domain-restricted search; all direct fetches blocked.

3.1.3.notes: Backup encryption is not documented anywhere on Replicate's public pages retrieved this session ('Not known' is the playbook-expected answer for most vendors here). Note the related mitigating control: API prediction inputs/outputs are auto-deleted after one hour by default (replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/data-retention), which limits what could be in backups at all. Searched same pages as 3.1.2.

3.1.4.notes: Since no encryption-at-rest standard or key-management scheme is documented at all (see 3.1.2), asserting the playbook's managed-cloud default 'Key generated by Subprocessor (not customer-specific)' would be inference, not evidence. No CMEK/BYOK offering was found either. Ask the vendor; also confirm with the human whether Tavus's Replicate arrangement involves any customer-managed keys (very unlikely for an inference API, but the playbook says check).

3.1.6.notes: No primary source states Replicate can anonymize customer personal data on the customer's instruction. Adjacent-but-different facts found (do not conflate): the privacy policy says Replicate 'may disclose de-identified, aggregate, or anonymous information about Website visitors' and the Terms define 'Resultant Data' as aggregated and anonymized usage data (replicate.com/privacy, replicate.com/terms) — that is Replicate anonymizing its own analytics data, not a processor capability offered over SAP/Tavus personal data. Searched replicate.com privacy/terms/docs via domain-restricted search.

3.1.7.notes: No mention of pseudonymization anywhere in retrieved Replicate material. Same search scope as 3.1.6.

3.2.1.notes: The test is 'does the vendor OFFER an EU region'. No Replicate page retrieved this session documents region selection, EU data residency, or where inference runs; the docs describe deployments/hardware choices but not geographic regions. Replicate runs on hyperscaler infrastructure that has EU regions, but that does not establish that Replicate offers EU processing to customers — 'Not known' is the only supportable answer. Post-Cloudflare-acquisition regionality plans (integration with Cloudflare's network) are also undocumented. Searched: replicate.com/docs (deployments, how-does-replicate-work), /enterprise, /privacy via domain-restricted search.

open_questions_for_vendor: Please confirm the exact current legal entity that contracts for the Replicate service (name, legal form, state of formation, and registered address) following the Cloudflare acquisition — is it Replicate, LLC, and is it a wholly-owned subsidiary of Cloudflare, Inc.? Your public pages show two addresses (101 Townsend Street, San Francisco, CA 94107 on replicate.com/privacy; 2261 Market Street #4056, San Francisco, CA 94114 on internal.replicate.com/privacy) — which is authoritative?
Has Replicate (or its Cloudflare parent, on Replicate's behalf) designated a representative in the EU under Article 27 GDPR? If yes, please provide the representative's name and full address.

Does Replicate have a formally appointed Data Protection Officer? If yes, please provide name, telephone number and/or email; if not, please confirm privacy@replicate.com as the contact entitled to respond to data-protection requests.

Which security certifications or audit reports does Replicate currently hold (SOC 2 Type II, SOC 1/3, ISO/IEC 27001, 27018, 27701, 22301, 9001)? Please provide the current reports/certificates. If Replicate is now covered under Cloudflare, Inc.'s compliance program, please state which certifications extend to the Replicate service and from what date.
What minimum TLS version is enforced for data in transit (a) on the public API endpoints (api.replicate.com) and (b) for internal traffic between services and model pods?

Is customer data (prediction inputs, outputs, files, logs, custom model weights) encrypted at rest, with which algorithm (e.g. AES-256), and on which underlying cloud provider(s) and region(s) is it stored?
Are backups of customer data taken, and if so are they encrypted and with which algorithm?
Who generates and manages the encryption keys for data at rest — Replicate/its cloud provider (shared or customer-specific keys), or can customers supply their own keys (CMEK/BYOK)?

Can Replicate anonymize and/or pseudonymize customer personal data on the customer's documented instruction (Art. 28(3)(e) GDPR support), as opposed to the aggregated/anonymized 'Resultant Data' described in your Terms?

Does Replicate offer an EU processing region or EU data residency option (inference executed and data stored within the EU/EEA)? If yes, how is it enabled and does it cover video/audio inference workloads?
